advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the HTML-comment loss guard multiplicity-aware (compare counts, e.g. `Counter(findall(md))` vs `Counter(findall(decoded))`) so dropped duplicate comments also trigger the plain-encode fallback.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py:439: `comments = _HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(md)`
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py:442: `if any(comment not in decoded for comment in comments):`

Docstring claim: 'a body that would lose one degrades to the plain encode, trading richness for content preservation' — but multiplicity loss (2 identical comments -> 1) is undetected since membership testing ignores counts.
advisory.finding: The HTML-comment loss guard in `markdown_to_adf` checks only for the PRESENCE of each comment string in the decoded output, not its multiplicity. `comments = _HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(md)` yields duplicates, but `any(comment not in decoded for comment in comments)` is False whenever at least one copy of an identical comment survives — so a body containing the same HTML comment multiple times, of which marklas drops some, will NOT degrade to the plain encode and silently loses content, defeating the guard's stated purpose.
scenarios: A description containing two or more identical HTML comments (e.g. a duplicated echo/marker block) where marklas drops one; the guard sees the surviving copy and does not degrade, so the wire silently loses a comment.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compare occurrence counts rather than membership: e.g. `from collections import Counter; if Counter(comments) - Counter(_HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(decoded)):` then degrade.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the `plain_text_adf_functions` docstring to say it returns a mapping/dict rather than 'a set'.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py:487: `"""Return the PLAIN (non-Markdown-aware) conversion functions as a set.`
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py:486: `def plain_text_adf_functions() -> dict[str, Any]:` — returns a mapping, not a set.
advisory.finding: `plain_text_adf_functions` docstring describes its return value as 'a set' ('Return the PLAIN ... conversion functions as a set'), but it returns a `dict[str, Any]`. The mismatch could mislead the story-3388 caller about the expected shape.
scenarios: A maintainer wiring the whole-codec swap in story 3388 reads 'a set' and expects set semantics.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a body whose comment marklas drops causes markdown_to_adf to return the plain text_to_adf encode (assert the fallback shape, not just marker survival)
evidence: adf.py:439-443: `comments = _HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(md)` ... `if any(comment not in decoded for comment in comments): return text_to_adf(md)`
test_adf_markdown.py:96-101 asserts only `marker in _roundtrip(...)`, never that a comment-dropping input returns `text_to_adf(md)`
ABSENCE: no test asserts markdown_to_adf(body_with_dropped_comment) == text_to_adf(body) — the branch's observable effect (plain encode) is never pinned
adf.py:465-471 docstring: 'inflates differently from markdown_to_adf — so a Markdown-aware wire fitted with the plain function can still exceed the cap'
test_adf_markdown.py:106 `fitted = adf.fit_markdown_to_adf_limit("z" * 100_000)` — no markdown structure
ABSENCE: no over-limit input containing headings/lists/code fences is fitted and asserted <= limit
advisory.finding: The documented HTML-comment content-loss defense in markdown_to_adf (decode its own output, compare source comments, degrade to text_to_adf when one would be dropped) is not directly verified. The only test of it, test_cloud_html_comment_survives, asserts the marker survives a round trip — which passes whether or not the degrade branch fires (trivially true if marklas preserves the marker). Deleting adf.py:440-443 would redden a test only IF marklas actually drops the marker, which no test independently establishes, so the defensive branch is regression-blind.
merged_from: fit_markdown_to_adf_limit is exercised only with structureless plain text ('z' * 100_000), so it never validates its stated rationale that Markdown-aware ADF inflates differently from plain text. The truncation of a body with real Markdown block structure (headings/lists/fences), where the serialized size behaves differently than plain text, is not asserted.
scenarios: A refactor that removes or breaks the self-verify comment check ships green because the round-trip assertion still passes when marklas happens to preserve markers
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches adf._marklas to a stub whose to_md drops the comment, and assert markdown_to_adf(body) == adf.text_to_adf(body).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests that stub _marklas to an engine whose to_adf/to_md raises, asserting markdown_to_adf/adf_to_markdown return their plain counterparts
evidence: adf.py:444-445 `except Exception: return text_to_adf(md)`
adf.py:460-461 `except Exception: return adf_to_text(doc)`
test_adf_markdown.py:113-120 only stubs `_marklas` to return None; ABSENCE: no test forces engine.to_adf/to_md to raise
advisory.finding: The `except Exception -> plain fallback` degradation branches in markdown_to_adf (adf.py:444-445) and adf_to_markdown (adf.py:460-461) are untested. test_cloud_functions_degrade_without_marklas only covers the `_marklas() is None` path; no test injects an engine that raises, so the conversion-error degradation contract (documented as 'any engine failure degrades, never propagates') has no regression coverage.
scenarios: A future change that lets an engine exception propagate (removing the try/except) would not be caught by any test
advisory.suggested_fix: monkeypatch adf._marklas to a fake module whose to_adf raises, and assert markdown_to_adf(md) == adf.text_to_adf(md) (and symmetrically for adf_to_markdown).
